summaries.body:
V14.2.1 merges three 4.0.3 controls that all forbade putting secrets in URLs. The mapping records MODIFIED, MOVED FROM v4.0.3-8.3.1, MERGED FROM v4.0.3-3.1.1, v4.0.3-13.1.3. V8.3.1 required sending sensitive data in the HTTP body or headers, not query-string parameters. V3.1.1 forbade session tokens in URL parameters. V13.1.3 forbade API URLs exposing API keys, session tokens, and similar.

The current clause unifies those: sensitive data only in the HTTP message body or header fields; URL and query string must not contain sensitive information such as an API key or session token. Git at V3.1.1 (abhay session-management CWEs, 2019-02-11) is a real predecessor line; V14.2.1-slot proactive-control ticks in 4.x Configuration are slot reuse for the current ID number.

The 5.0 merge is the wording change that mattered: three overlapping URL-secrecy checks became one body-or-headers rule that names both API keys and session tokens. On the V3.1.1 line, tghosth edited Session Management markdown (2019-02-19, 2019-02-25) and jim did so again on 2020-07-13. vanderaj's 2018-11-18 Grammarly pass on V3.1.1 is editorial.

V14.2.1-slot events (proactive-control marking, 2020 URL corrections) are 4.x Configuration ID reuse and should not be read as rewriting this data-protection clause.
